html:
Professional long-distance traders of the Aztec Empire. The pochteca formed hereditary guilds, based above all in Tlatelolco, the market twin of Tenochtitlan, and in a few other cities.

They led caravans of porters on foot, since Mesoamerica had no draft animals. They carried cloth, obsidian and metal goods south and came back with luxuries: cacao, quetzal feathers, jade, jaguar skins and gold. Their routes reached the Gulf Coast, Soconusco on the Pacific and the lands of the Maya.

The pochteca also served the state. Some travelled in disguise as spies, and their reports could start a war. An attack on merchants was a common reason for conquest.

They had their own god, Yacatecuhtli, their own courts and their own feasts. Wealthy as they were, they hid their riches to avoid the envy of the nobles. Much of what we know about them comes from the Florentine Codex of Bernardino de Sahagún.
sum: Professional long-distance traders of the Aztec Empire. The pochteca formed hereditary guilds, based above all in Tlatelolco, the market twin of Tenochtitlan, and in a few other cities.
